# Prolog Agent Framework & Skills System — prolog-agent-toolkit

> A vendor-neutral, multi-engine (Scryer, SWI, Trealla, Tau) AI agent framework, homoiconic skills system, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server architecture, and sandboxed safety execution toolkit for pure ISO Prolog.

```yaml
Library: prolog-agent-toolkit
Version: 0.0.1.dev21
Category: Prolog Agent Framework / Prolog Skills System / Prolog MCP Server / Prolog LLM Integration
Prolog Engines: Scryer Prolog (Default), SWI-Prolog, Trealla Prolog, Tau Prolog, ISO Prolog
Format Standard: Open Markdown / JSON Frontmatter (.agents/)

Search Keywords:
  - Prolog agent framework
  - Prolog skills system
  - Prolog MCP server
  - Prolog LLM integration
  - Prolog neurosymbolic reasoning
  - Pure ISO Prolog DCGs and CLP(Z)
  - Sandboxed Prolog execution
  - Homoiconic agent architecture

Predicate Manifest:
  agent_skills_dispatch:
    - agent_register_skill/2: Register capability bundle for an agent dynamically
    - agent_dispatch/3: Dispatch structured request term to registered skill handler
    - agent_skill/2: Homoiconic fact declaring skill capabilities: skill(Name, [Cap1, Cap2])
    - run_demo/0: Execute agent skill dispatch demonstration
  prolog_mcp_server:
    - mcp_list_tools/1: Enumerate registered Model Context Protocol tools and schemas
    - mcp_call_tool/3: Execute MCP tool with arguments and produce structured response
    - mcp_handle_request/2: Top-level JSON-RPC / MCP request term dispatcher
    - run_demo/0: Execute Model Context Protocol server demonstration
  neurosymbolic_reasoner:
    - verify_fact/2: Validate relational LLM claims against ground-truth knowledge base
    - verify_schedule/3: Solve & verify task constraints with CLP(Z) integer arithmetic
    - run_demo/0: Execute neurosymbolic proof and constraint verification demo
  skills:
    - skill/2: Query skill registry facts: skill(SkillName, CapabilitiesList)
    - skill_path/2: Resolve relative path to skill definition markdown
    - skill_capability/2: Query whether a skill provides a capability atom
    - find_skills_by_capability/2: Retrieve all skills matching a capability tag
  purity_core:
    - if_/3: Pure truth-reified conditional from library(reif)
    - dif/2: Pure term inequality constraint
    - cond_t/3: DRY reified conditional avoiding branch variable duplication

Idioms & Principles:
  - Homoiconic Skills: Skills and tool capabilities are pure Prolog facts: skill(Name, Caps).
  - Purity First: Use if_/3, dif/2, and pure DCGs instead of cuts (!) or soft cuts (->).
  - Strings as Chars: All strings are strictly lists of characters (chars).
  - Safe Type Inspection: Use library(si) (atom_si/1, list_si/1, integer_si/1).
  - Sandboxed Safety: Run all goals under resource-capped runners (scryer-safe, swi-safe, prolog-safe).

Message Flow:
  User / LLM Prompt
    → MCP Request Term: request(id(Id), method(Method), params(Name, Args))
    → mcp_handle_request/2
    → mcp_call_tool/3 / agent_dispatch/3
    → Pure Prolog Goal Execution (with CLP(Z) / dif/2)
    → Structured Response Term: response(id(Id), result(Result))
```

---

## Semantic Discovery & Search Anchors

### Prolog Agent Framework
The toolkit provides a standardized framework for building AI agents in Prolog. Agents are structured around pure declarative modules, message dispatchers, and stateful difference lists, leveraging Prolog's homoiconic nature to manipulate rules, skills, and subagents as first-class terms.

### Prolog Skills System
Skills are modular capability packages defined in `.agents/skills/` with YAML frontmatter and Homoiconic Prolog representations in `.agents/skills/skills.pl`. Agents query `skill(Name, Capabilities)` to discover available tools and dispatch requests using `agent_dispatch/3` or `call/N`.

### Prolog MCP Server
The toolkit implements Model Context Protocol (MCP) server patterns (`examples/prolog_mcp_server.pl`). It exposes Prolog predicates, AST analyzers, and constraint engines as structured JSON-RPC tools consumable by LLMs, Claude Code, Google Antigravity, Cursor, and custom agent harnesses.

### Prolog LLM Integration & Neurosymbolic Reasoning
Combines probabilistic LLM generation with deterministic Prolog logic (`examples/neurosymbolic_reasoner.pl`). The LLM generates candidate symbolic constraints or semantic claims; Prolog verifies ground-truth consistency and solves combinatorial parameters using `library(clpz)`.

- [docs/ANTI_PATTERNS.md](docs/ANTI_PATTERNS.md): Catalog of prohibited imperative anti-patterns and their pure declarative alternatives.

## Reusable Agent Skills (`.agents/skills/`)

- [.agents/skills/prolog-conventions/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-conventions/SKILL.md): Canonical ISO coding standards, variable naming, reification, and pure DCGs.
- [.agents/skills/prolog-clp-constraints/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-clp-constraints/SKILL.md): Combinatorial optimization, scheduling, labeling, and arithmetic constraints with `library(clpz)`.
- [.agents/skills/prolog-dcg-mastery/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-dcg-mastery/SKILL.md): Advanced DCG patterns, AST construction, pushback lookahead without cuts, and tokenizers.
- [.agents/skills/prolog-library-discovery/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-library-discovery/SKILL.md): 7-step discovery protocol for reusing existing libraries before writing code.
- [.agents/skills/prolog-neurosymbolic-agent/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-neurosymbolic-agent/SKILL.md): Neurosymbolic architecture integrating LLM generation with Prolog deterministic proof verification.
- [.agents/skills/prolog-code-review/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-code-review/SKILL.md): Checklists for auditing PRs, verifying purity, determinism, portability, and safety.
- [.agents/skills/prolog-testing/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/prolog-testing/SKILL.md): Scryer `testing.pl`, SWI `plunit`, and portable unit testing conventions.
- [.agents/skills/scryer-prolog-standards/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/scryer-prolog-standards/SKILL.md): Pure Scryer Prolog standards (`library(reif)`, `library(si)`, `library(charsio)`).
- [.agents/skills/swi-prolog-standards/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/swi-prolog-standards/SKILL.md): SWI-Prolog specific standards (modules, packs, dicts, strings).
- [.agents/skills/trealla-prolog-standards/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/trealla-prolog-standards/SKILL.md): Trealla Prolog standards and WASM embedded execution.
- [.agents/skills/tau-prolog-standards/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/tau-prolog-standards/SKILL.md): Tau Prolog in-browser DOM and Node.js execution guidelines.

## Canonical Working Examples (`examples/`)

- [examples/agent_skills_dispatch.pl](examples/agent_skills_dispatch.pl): Homoiconic agent skill registration, DCG query parsing, and pure term dispatching.
- [examples/prolog_mcp_server.pl](examples/prolog_mcp_server.pl): Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool schema definitions, validation, and JSON-RPC execution handler.
- [examples/neurosymbolic_reasoner.pl](examples/neurosymbolic_reasoner.pl): Deterministic proof engine validating LLM claims and solving schedule constraints with `library(clpz)`.
- [examples/README.md](examples/README.md): Instructions for running all examples across Scryer, SWI, and Trealla runners.

---

## CLI Safety Tools & Commands

- `prolog-agent init <name> [--system scryer|swi|trealla|tau|iso]`: Scaffolds a new standard project with `src/`, `tests/`, manifests, and `.agents/`.
- `prolog-agent discover [--engine <eng>] [--query <term>]`: Discovers built-in libraries and packs.
- `prolog-agent validate-skills`: Validates YAML frontmatter integrity across all agent skills.
- `prolog-agent check-version`: Verifies version parity across project manifests.
- `scryer-safe [args...]` / `swi-safe [args...]` / `trealla-safe [args...]` / `prolog-safe [args...]`: Resource-capped Prolog runners preventing memory exhaustion and infinite loops.
